requirement: FedRAMP scope (FedRAMP Authorization Act, 44 U.S.C. 3614; OMB M-24-15 Section III)
applies_when: A cloud product or service creates, collects, processes, stores or maintains Federal information on behalf of a Federal agency and is not in an excluded category. Excluded categories include widely available services that provide information to agencies without collecting Federal information, and ancillary negligible-risk services. The agency makes the final determination.
what_it_requires: Agencies must use a FedRAMP-certified offering for in-scope cloud services.
design_implication: Tier 0 (open data) and Tier 1 (static explorer) must never collect Federal information: no uploads, no accounts, no server-side processing of what users type, no query logs. Agencies then consume EMST as a public information provider, outside FedRAMP scope. A hosted tool holding agency personnel data (Tier 3) would be in scope.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now: an architectural rule costs nothing at design time; costly later: certifying a hosted SaaS takes a funded provider, continuous monitoring and an assessor

requirement: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026 (CR26) and FedRAMP 20x: Certification Classes A-D; Program path without an agency sponsor
applies_when: Only if EMST or a partner ever offers a hosted multi-tenant service to agencies (Tier 3).
what_it_requires: Certification by class. Class A is presumed adequate for pilots or for negligible-risk uses such as processing public information. Class B maps to legacy Low and Class C to legacy Moderate. CR26 rules took effect for new 20x certifications on 2026-07-04, become mandatory for existing certifications on 2027-01-01, and new Rev5 certifications stop on 2027-06-11. Machine-readable packages and Key Security Indicators replace control narratives.
design_implication: Do not build Tier 3 in the pilot or MVP. If a hosted service is ever needed, either (a) partner with an already-certified platform that agencies use (their HCM or LMS) or (b) build cloud-native and infrastructure-as-code from day one so 20x evidence is machine-generated. 'Certified' is replacing 'Authorized', so use current terms in procurement language.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: costly later if built ad hoc; cheap now to defer

requirement: FISMA (44 U.S.C. 3551 et seq.) and agency Authorization to Operate (NIST SP 800-37 RMF; OMB Circular A-130)
applies_when: An information system is used or operated by an agency, or by a contractor or other organization on behalf of an agency.
what_it_requires: Security categorization, a security and privacy plan, assessment, AO risk acceptance (ATO) and continuous monitoring.
design_implication: Keep the EMST steward independent: an NGO or university operating open public infrastructure, not operating 'on behalf of' any agency. Agencies that rehost the static site or run Tier 2 kits do so on platforms they have already authorized (existing CMS or static hosting; analytics enclave; HCM or LMS). Publish an 'agency security packet' (data-flow diagram showing no PII, SBOM, dependency list, hosting description) so the agency can treat adoption as a minor change inside an existing boundary, not a new ATO.

requirement: OMB M-26-05 Adopting a Risk-based Approach to Software and Hardware Security (Jan 23 2026), which rescinds M-22-18 and M-23-16
applies_when: Agencies acquire or use software, including open-source code and downloadable data packages they run.
what_it_requires: Each agency sets its own risk-based software assurance policy. The CISA Secure Software Development Attestation Form is available but optional. Agencies may require an SBOM on request. NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF) is a reference. Complete software and hardware inventories remain mandatory.
design_implication: There is no longer a single federal attestation to satisfy, so expect 20+ different agency questionnaires. Pre-answer them: publish an SSDF practice mapping, a voluntarily completed CISA attestation form, an SBOM per release, and checksums for every release asset, so agencies can inventory exactly what they took.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now: about 2 days of work; costly later: answering bespoke agency questionnaires one by one

requirement: Software Bill of Materials (CISA 2025 draft Minimum Elements for an SBOM, offered as guidance under M-26-05)
applies_when: An agency or state asks for an SBOM, or runs EMST site code or Tier 2 kits.
what_it_requires: A machine-readable SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX) listing components and versions.
design_implication: Generate an SBOM in release CI for the site bundle and each kit. Keep the JavaScript dependency tree small (this is a selection criterion for the static site generator). Data-only releases list their schema and validator versions.

requirement: OpenSSF Scorecard and supply-chain hygiene (voluntary)
applies_when: Always, for the public repository. State and federal reviewers and vendors increasingly read the score.
what_it_requires: Automated checks: Pinned-Dependencies, Token-Permissions, Signed-Releases, SBOM, Branch-Protection, Code-Review, Security-Policy, Dangerous-Workflow, Dependency-Update-Tool, Vulnerabilities.
design_implication: Run the Scorecard Action from day one. Pin GitHub Actions by commit SHA (the OpenLMP release workflow pins by tag, @v4). Use least-privilege tokens per job, signed tags and releases with build-provenance attestations, Dependabot or Renovate, branch protection with required review, and SECURITY.md with a disclosure address.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: retrofitting after a supply-chain incident

requirement: CISA Secure by Design principles and pledge (voluntary)
applies_when: The project publishes software that government uses.
what_it_requires: Secure defaults, a vulnerability disclosure policy, transparent CVE handling, and taking ownership of security outcomes.
design_implication: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and security.txt, keep secure defaults (no third-party scripts, no tracking), and publish a security changelog per release.

requirement: Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a): systems of records, SORNs, Privacy Act statements
applies_when: A federal agency maintains records about individuals that it retrieves by name or another personal identifier. Employee skills profiles, self-assessments, IDPs and team gap analyses all qualify once stored in an agency system.
what_it_requires: A published SORN covering the records and their routine uses; a Privacy Act statement at collection; access and amendment rights; limits on disclosure; accounting of disclosures.
design_implication: EMST never holds person-level records. The browser-based gap check keeps answers on the user's device and saves only to a file the user controls. Tier 2 kits run inside agency systems already covered by a SORN (for example a government-wide personnel or talent SORN, or the agency's LMS SORN; FH and agency privacy offices to confirm coverage). Each kit ships a data-element inventory so the privacy office can check SORN coverage quickly. The public site never retrieves anything by personal identifier.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: a new SORN needs Federal Register notice and comment and typically takes months

requirement: E-Government Act of 2002 Section 208 PIAs (OMB M-03-22); Privacy Threshold Analyses
applies_when: An agency develops or procures IT that collects, maintains or disseminates PII, or uses AI that processes PII.
what_it_requires: A PTA to screen, then a PIA where PII is present. Agency websites need privacy policies.
design_implication: Ship a PTA and PIA starter text with each Tier 2 kit (data elements, purposes, retention, sharing, AI use). Publish a privacy notice on the public site that says plainly that no personal data is collected, with the technical reasons (no cookies, no server, local storage only).

requirement: Controlled Unclassified Information, Privacy category (32 CFR 2002; NIST SP 800-171)
applies_when: Agency personnel data (rosters, assessments, IDPs, performance data) is shared with a non-federal party such as the EMST team, a pilot NGO or a contractor.
what_it_requires: Safeguarding under the agency's CUI program, generally NIST SP 800-171 controls for non-federal systems, and a written agreement.
design_implication: Standing rule: the EMST team does not accept agency personnel data, not even for 'pilot analysis'. Pilot analyses use public PDs and postings, synthetic examples, or aggregates that the agency de-identifies and computes inside its own systems with EMST kits.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: a single spreadsheet of employee ratings in a shared drive creates a CUI incident

requirement: Federal Records Act and NARA rules (44 U.S.C. ch. 31 and 33; 36 CFR ch. XII subch. B)
applies_when: Agency staff create PDs, IDPs, training plans or workforce analyses with EMST.
what_it_requires: Agency records must be kept in agency recordkeeping systems under approved schedules.
design_implication: All outputs export as files (accessible PDF, DOCX, CSV, JSON) that the user saves into agency systems; EMST keeps no copy. Every export is stamped with the EMST release ID and DOI so the record shows exactly which version of the taxonomy was used (also supports later defensibility).

requirement: Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.; 5 CFR 1320)
applies_when: A federal agency conducts or sponsors a collection of identical questions from 10 or more persons in 12 months. State, local and NGO staff count as persons. Federal employees and military acting in their role do not. Direct observation and non-standardized interviews are generally not 'information'.
what_it_requires: OMB clearance (an information collection request takes about 9 to 12 months) or use of an existing generic clearance.
design_implication: Run pilot user research under NGO or coalition sponsorship, not on behalf of an agency. Where a federal agency co-sponsors, use direct observation and semi-structured interviews, keep standardized questionnaires (SUS, UMUX-Lite) to federal-employee participants or under fewer than 10 non-federal respondents, or use the agency's generic clearance. Any in-product feedback form on a federally hosted copy needs PRA review.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: a 9-12 month ICR delay to the federal phase

requirement: Federal web analytics and cookies (OMB M-10-22 tiers; GSA Digital Analytics Program)
applies_when: An agency rehosts the EMST site on a .gov domain or embeds it.
what_it_requires: No PII in analytics; IP anonymization; privacy notice for persistent cookies; DAP participation for public federal sites.
design_implication: MVP ships with no analytics script at all. The site is built so a federal host can add DAP through a single include without code changes. Never put user inputs (role choices, ratings) in URLs or query strings, because they would leak into server and analytics logs.

requirement: Digital identity (NIST SP 800-63) and Login.gov
applies_when: The product offers user accounts to the public or to federal staff.
what_it_requires: Identity proofing and authentication assurance appropriate to risk; account data becomes a system of records.
design_implication: No accounts in Tiers 0-1. Saved work is a local file. This avoids identity, authentication and account-record obligations entirely.

requirement: OMB M-25-21 (Apr 3 2025): high-impact AI minimum risk practices
applies_when: An agency's AI output is a principal basis for decisions with legal, material, binding or significant effects, including on access to employment; such uses are presumed high-impact.
what_it_requires: Seven minimum practices: pre-deployment testing, an AI impact assessment, ongoing monitoring, human training and assessment, human oversight and accountability, remedies or appeals, and end-user and public consultation. These were due within 365 days unless waived by the Chief AI Officer. Agencies must also inventory AI use cases.
design_implication: Design every AI feature as decision support that a named human adopts or rejects. Never rank, score or screen people. Ship an impact-assessment input pack with any AI feature (intended use, out-of-scope uses, evaluation results by subgroup where possible, failure modes, human-review UI) so an agency can complete its assessment and inventory entry quickly.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: retrofitting oversight and evaluation into a deployed feature

requirement: OPM CHCO memo 'Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Hiring Process' (Aug 27 2026)
applies_when: A federal agency uses AI in any hiring step, including drafting PDs, qualification requirements and interview questions.
what_it_requires: AI drafting of PDs and qualifications is generally not high-impact if officials review, revise and adopt the drafts (documented to the CAIO). Ratifying AI output without real review makes the use high-impact. AI-assisted steps remain subject to job analysis and validation under 5 CFR 300.103. Applicant data must be processed only in authorized tools, and actions must be documented and auditable.
design_implication: The PD builder is positioned as a drafting aid: every generated duty statement traces to EMST task and competency IDs (job-analysis linkage), and the UI requires an explicit human 'adopt or edit' step and records it. The builder never takes applicant data. This lets an HR office use it under the 'generally not high-impact' path.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; a strong adoption lever with FH

requirement: OMB M-25-22 (Apr 3 2025): AI acquisition
applies_when: An agency contracts for an AI system or service; applies to solicitations issued on or after Sep 30 2025.
what_it_requires: Government data rights; vendors may not train on non-public agency data without explicit consent; terms that prevent vendor lock-in; testing and monitoring rights.
design_implication: Keep EMST content openly licensed and vendor-neutral so it can sit in any vendor's skills engine, and so agencies can require 'EMST-compatible' interfaces without lock-in. EMST-run services must never receive agency data, so no data-rights clause is ever needed with the EMST steward.

requirement: OMB M-26-04 Unbiased AI Principles (Dec 11 2025; sunsets after two years unless extended)
applies_when: An agency procures an LLM. Free open-source LLMs are not subject but need due diligence.
what_it_requires: Solicitations must require an acceptable use policy, model, system or data cards, end-user resources and a mechanism for reporting outputs that violate the principles of truth-seeking (including acknowledging uncertainty) and ideological neutrality.
design_implication: If Tier 2 kits include prompts or pipelines for an agency's LLM, ship a system card (purpose, prompts, evaluation set, known failure modes, uncertainty handling) and a feedback route. Disclose LLM involvement in EMST content creation (v1 coding was LLM-assisted) in provenance fields.

requirement: Selection-use boundary: Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR 1607); 5 CFR 300.103; merit system principles
applies_when: EMST outputs (gap scores, proficiency ratings, competency lists) are used to select, promote or screen people.
what_it_requires: Job analysis, validity evidence, adverse-impact monitoring and documentation.
design_implication: Label the product 'for development and planning; not a selection instrument'. No person-ranking or pass/fail outputs. Gap check results are framed as development priorities. Selection use requires agency-run validation (IO and FH lane), and the product links to that guidance instead of enabling it.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: defending an unvalidated tool in an adverse-impact challenge

requirement: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 794d; revised ICT standards, 36 CFR 1194, incorporating WCAG 2.0 Level AA)
applies_when: A federal agency develops, procures, maintains or uses ICT, including content it links, embeds or rehosts.
what_it_requires: WCAG 2.0 AA conformance for web content and documents. Agencies ask vendors and projects for an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT).
design_implication: Conform to WCAG 2.2 AA, a superset that satisfies 508's WCAG 2.0 AA and Title II's 2.1 AA. Publish an ACR (VPAT 2.5 or later, 508 and WCAG editions) for each major release. Exports (PDF, DOCX) must also be accessible: tagged PDFs, real headings, table headers.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: retrofitting charts and PDFs after launch

requirement: WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation 2023-10-05, updated 2024-12-12; ISO/IEC 40500:2025); WCAG 3 draft
applies_when: Always; this is the target standard.
what_it_requires: WCAG 2.2 adds 9 success criteria over 2.1, including Focus Not Obscured (2.4.11), Dragging Movements (2.5.7), Target Size Minimum (2.5.8), Consistent Help (3.2.6), Redundant Entry (3.3.7) and Accessible Authentication (3.3.8). There will be no WCAG 2.3. WCAG 3 is an incomplete draft (Sept 2026) that is years from completion. EN 301 549 (2026) uses WCAG 2.2.
design_implication: Gap check and pathway map must not rely on drag or hover: provide button or keyboard alternatives and 24x24 px minimum targets. Do not ask users to re-enter answers (the role chosen carries through all views). Keep the sticky header from obscuring focus. Do not build toward WCAG 3 yet.

requirement: 21st Century IDEA (Pub. L. 115-336) and OMB M-23-22 'Delivering a Digital-First Public Experience' (current status not verified for Oct 2026)
applies_when: A federal agency publishes or rehosts a public website.
what_it_requires: USWDS-consistent design, accessibility, mobile-friendly design, search, privacy, .gov domains, analytics.
design_implication: Build on USWDS 3.x design tokens and components (current release 3.14.0, Aug 2026) so an agency can rehost on .gov without redesign, and so federal users see familiar patterns.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: a redesign to adopt

requirement: Section 504 web accessibility rule for HHS funding recipients (45 CFR 84, 2024; WCAG 2.1 AA)
applies_when: A state agency, local government or NGO (including pilot organizations) receives HHS financial assistance and uses or provides EMST content. Other federal agencies' Section 504 rules may follow.
what_it_requires: WCAG 2.1 AA web and mobile accessibility. The first compliance date of May 11 2026 was not extended as of April 2026.
design_implication: Covered by the WCAG 2.2 AA target. Tell pilot NGOs that they may already be bound through their grants.

requirement: ADA Title II web and mobile accessibility rule (28 CFR 35.200; 2024 final rule; compliance dates extended by DOJ interim final rule of Apr 20 2026)
applies_when: A state or local government (including special districts and public universities) provides or makes available web content or apps, including content provided through vendors or licensors.
what_it_requires: WCAG 2.1 AA, now by Apr 26 2027 (population 50,000 or more) and Apr 26 2028 (under 50,000, and special districts). The IFR did not change the substance. DOJ signalled possible future rulemaking on the substance. A private right of action creates litigation risk, and existing Title II obligations continue meanwhile.
design_implication: EMST conformance protects state and local adopters who embed or link EMST views. Publish the ACR and an accessibility statement with a contact route. Watch DOJ's further rulemaking (comments closed Jun 22 2026).

requirement: State digital accessibility laws (e.g., Colorado HB 21-1110; California Gov. Code 7405 and 11135; others)
applies_when: State agencies procure, build or use ICT. Some laws reach local governments and vendors.
what_it_requires: Typically WCAG 2.1 AA or 508 alignment, accessibility plans, and procurement clauses; some include private enforcement.
design_implication: WCAG 2.2 AA and a published ACR satisfy most procurement asks [J]. SL to build a state-by-state table for pilot states.

requirement: State cloud security verification: GovRAMP (formerly StateRAMP), TX-RAMP, AZRAMP and similar
applies_when: A state or local agency procures a cloud service that stores or processes state data.
what_it_requires: Third-party verified security posture at a defined level before purchase or renewal.
design_implication: Tiers 0-1 hold no state data and are not procured, so these programs should not apply [J]; confirm with one pilot state CISO. A Tier 3 hosted tool would need GovRAMP and possibly state-specific programs, which is another reason not to build one.

requirement: State IT security reviews of third-party web content (state CISO policies, mostly NIST SP 800-53-based)
applies_when: State staff use or embed an external site; state networks filter third-party scripts and trackers.
what_it_requires: Reviews of third-party scripts, cookies, embeds and data flows.
design_implication: No third-party requests at runtime: self-host fonts (the OpenLMP dashboard loads Google Fonts) and do not use embedded SaaS widgets (Flourish, GitBook). Add a Content-Security-Policy through a meta tag, because GitHub Pages cannot set response headers [J]. Use Subresource Integrity if any asset ever comes from a CDN.

requirement: State public-employee data laws (e.g., Minnesota Government Data Practices Act; California Information Practices Act; state public records acts)
applies_when: A state or local agency stores employee self-assessments, IDPs or team gap analyses produced with EMST kits.
what_it_requires: Classification of the data (public, private or confidential); access rights; disclosure under public records requests, which can expose employee data that is not protected.
design_implication: Tier 2 kits default to aggregated team views with a minimum cell size (for example 5 or more) and keep individual ratings with the individual. Kit documentation warns that stored individual ratings may be disclosable under state public records law and must be classified by the agency.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: a records request exposing staff self-ratings would end adoption in that state

requirement: State AI-in-employment and government-AI laws (Colorado AI Act SB 24-205 as delayed; Illinois HB 3773; California Civil Rights Council ADS regulations; NYC Local Law 144; Texas TRAIGA). Status as of Oct 2026 not verified
applies_when: AI is used to make, or as a substantial factor in, employment decisions (hiring, promotion, discipline, pay); some laws impose disclosure duties on government entities that use AI with the public.
what_it_requires: Varies: impact assessments, notices, bias audits, appeal rights, recordkeeping, disclosure of AI interaction.
design_implication: Same development-use boundary as CR-19. Any AI-assisted feature discloses that AI is involved and what it did. No automated consequential decisions. Keep documentation in a form that can feed an impact assessment. SL to verify the current status of each law for the pilot states before the federal and state phase.

requirement: State comprehensive consumer privacy laws that reach nonprofits (e.g., Colorado Privacy Act; Oregon Consumer Privacy Act)
applies_when: An NGO steward or pilot organization processes personal data of state residents above the law's thresholds.
what_it_requires: Notice, consumer rights, data protection assessments for some processing.
design_implication: No collection means no obligations. If a feedback or newsletter form is ever added, collect email only, publish a notice, and keep the form off the analytical site.

requirement: Open licensing and federal reuse (OPEN Government Data Act; 17 U.S.C. 105; agencies' open-data policies)
applies_when: Agencies republish, embed or modify EMST data in their own systems and open-data catalogs.
what_it_requires: Agency data assets in machine-readable form under open licenses. Federal works are not copyrightable.
design_implication: Resolve v1's contradiction (the GitHub CC0 selection vs the README's 'CC BY 4.0'). Recommend CC0 for data and vocabularies (no attribution chain when embedded in HCM or LMS systems; matches OpenLMP), CC BY 4.0 or CC0 for narrative documentation, and Apache-2.0 for code. Record the licence in every release's metadata.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: relicensing after contributors join requires their consent

requirement: Third-party content licences inside EMST (O*NET CC BY 4.0; ESCO; Lightcast Open Skills; vendor taxonomies; state class specifications)
applies_when: EMST copies or derives text from external taxonomies or datasets.
what_it_requires: Attribution (CC BY), share-alike or non-commercial terms, or prohibition of redistribution.
design_implication: Keep a third-party licence register. Crosswalks store external IDs and match types, not copied text, wherever possible. Never ingest licensed job-posting data (for example Lightcast) into the open repo except as permitted aggregates. The CC0 dedication must exclude third-party material.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: having to strip derived text from a release

requirement: Indigenous data governance (CARE Principles; Tribal laws and consultation policies; TN protocol)
applies_when: Content concerns Tribal knowledge, Tribal programs or Tribal employees; Tribal nations adopt kits.
what_it_requires: Collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility and ethics; Tribal law governs Tribal government employee data.
design_implication: Product-level guard: content carries a governance flag, and flagged content is excluded from open builds unless TN's protocol records consent. Tribal adopters run Tier 2 kits under their own governance. Nothing Tribal-specific appears on the public site by default.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: removing published content that was never ours to publish

requirement: Demand-signal inputs that contain personal data (PDs with incumbent names or position numbers; job postings; plan documents with contact details)
applies_when: IA and LM ingest PDs, postings or plans to detect change signals.
what_it_requires: Data minimization; the source's terms of use; Privacy Act obligations if an agency supplies records.
design_implication: Strip names, emails, phone numbers and position numbers at ingestion. Store only derived signals plus source URLs and hashes. Never store applicant data.

requirement: AI inference of skills from individuals' documents (resumes, self-descriptions, performance narratives)
applies_when: A feature infers a person's skills or proficiency from text about that person.
what_it_requires: Combines CR-08, CR-15, CR-16, CR-19 and CR-29: SORN and PIA if run by an agency; possible high-impact AI status; validation if used in selection; state AI-employment duties; sensitive-inference risk (for example age, disability or national-origin proxies).
design_implication: Not in the MVP. If it is ever offered, it is offered only as a Tier 2 kit running in the adopter's authorized environment (including its approved LLM). Every inferred skill needs the person's confirmation. The kit shows the evidence span for each suggestion, stores nothing by default, and comes with error rates measured on a hand-checked set, including by subgroup where possible.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now to defer; costly later if launched without controls

requirement: NGO pilot organizations' duties to their staff (employment law, confidentiality, state privacy law, grant terms)
applies_when: Pilot NGOs use the gap check for staff development.
what_it_requires: Fair treatment, confidentiality, and any grant-imposed data and accessibility terms.
design_implication: Local-first gap check: individuals own their ratings. Team views are built from files that individuals choose to share, with a consent note. A pilot data-use template (AS) says that EMST receives only de-identified synthesized findings.

requirement: Human subjects protections (Common Rule, 45 CFR 46) for pilot evaluation
applies_when: Pilot evaluation is federally funded or conducted and is designed to produce generalizable knowledge (for example CM's theory-of-change study or publications).
what_it_requires: IRB review or an exemption determination; informed consent.
design_implication: Keep usability research (product improvement) separate from evaluation research. Get an IRB determination through an academic partner before any outcome study that will be published.
cheap_now_or_costly_later: cheap now; costly later: unusable data for publication

requirement: Agency staff participation on GitHub (agency-negotiated federal-compatible terms of service; agency social media and public engagement policies)
applies_when: Agency staff comment on issues, propose changes or contribute data in their official capacity on the public repository.
what_it_requires: Agencies generally need approved terms of service and official-capacity guidance before staff use third-party platforms.
design_implication: Provide a non-GitHub route for official comments (email to the steward, or structured comment periods) so participation does not hinge on each agency's GitHub approval. Document contributor licence terms (DCO) up front.

requirement: Releases as citable, immutable versions (records, defensibility and reproducibility)
applies_when: Agencies cite EMST in PDs, training plans, curricula or workforce plans.
what_it_requires: Ability to show which version was used and what changed.
design_implication: Semantic versioning, signed tags, a DOI per release (for example via Zenodo), a delta file, persistent IDs with retained, replaced and withdrawn status. The site shows the release ID on every page and in every export.
